newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek govt raises 5.3 bln sum in '96 cash sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek govt raises 5.3 bln sum in '96 cash sell-off.

text.p: Uzbekistan's government raised 5.29 billion sum from cash privatisation last year, up from 2.38 billion in 1995, the State Property Committee said.

A report from the committee said 1,915 state-run companies were privatised for cash last year as part of a sell-off scheme started in 1993. This brings the total number of firms privatised in the Central Asian country to 4,194.
"Privatisation has allowed us to eliminate the monopoly of state property," Viktor Chzhen, Deputy Prime Minister and head of the property committee, said on Wednesday.
He told a government meeting that the private sector had started playing "an increasingly important role in creating the country's gross domestic product (GDP)."

Official statistics say the private sector accounts for more than 50 percent of industrial output and 98 percent of agricultural output. It provides jobs for more than 70 percent of those engaged in the national economy.
